i.norm: Verifies that the raw flags byte is preserved after parsing local file data even when the data buffer is too short to contain the timestamp indicated by the flags. Setup: - byte[3] with ACCESS_TIME_BIT (0x02) placed at index 2 - parseFromLocalFileData called with offset=2 and length=2 - The parser reads the flags byte at data[2] = 0x02 (ACCESS_TIME_BIT set) - Only 1 byte remains after the flags byte, which is insufficient for a 4-byte timestamp - The access-time-present boolean is cleared, but the flags field itself stays at 0x02
Place ACCESS_TIME_BIT in the byte that will be read as the flags byte (index 2).
Parse starting at offset 2 with length 2: only data[2] and data[3] would be in scope, but data[3] is out of bounds — effectively only 1 byte of content (the flags) is present.
Although the access timestamp itself could not be read (insufficient data), the raw flags byte should still reflect the value that was stored in the buffer.
